name: canonical category constants include supported and known unsupported keys
evidence: Exact supported-key order, known unsupported hairspray and German labels are the public category/schema vocabulary, consumed by productIntakeCategorySchema and Discovery category registries. Dropping scalp_care/heat_protectant or exposing the wrong label fails these independent literals; category alias tests do not pin supported membership/order.

name: normalizeCategoryKey maps production labels, canonical keys, and simple oil aliases
evidence: Each existing alias/canonical-key input drives the real map, including German/English and oil spellings and unknown→null. Removing only the Scalp Care or Oele alias can leave all direct vocabulary constants and unrelated intake fixtures green. No same-input composed keeper covers this full union.

name: normalizeText folds accents, punctuation, case, and spacing

assertions.text: assert.equal(normalizeText("  Öl / Leave-in -- Nº 5  "), "ol leave in no 5")

evidence: Actual normalizeText wrapper must fold the two exact punctuation/diacritic/number cases to fixed text. Returning raw text or dropping Nº normalization fails; the standalone normalizeIdentityText fixtures do not exercise this wrapper with these inputs. No new case is warranted just to retire it.

name: normalizeIdentityText is stable for case, whitespace, punctuation, and safe diacritics

assertions.text: assert.equal(normalizeIdentityText("  OLAPLEX   Nº. 5 -- Leave-In  "), "olaplex no 5 leave in")

assert.equal(
    normalizeIdentityText("OLAPLEX N°5 Bond Maintenance"),
    "olaplex no 5 bond maintenance",
  )
assert.equal(normalizeIdentityText("Olaplex No 5 Leave In"), "olaplex no 5 leave in")

evidence: Four exact strings independently require case/spacing/hyphen/slash folding and º/° number handling while retaining word order. Removing the degree-symbol No rewrite fails the N°5 input even though plain No and apostrophe cases pass. Identity matching and prompt preparation use this shared normalizer.

name: normalizeIdentityText matches L'Oreal variants without broad unsafe rewrites
evidence: Straight, curly and modifier-letter apostrophes plus bare Loreal must coalesce to loreal. The resolver punctuation keeper exercises only straight apostrophe, and its token regex differs from the direct normalizer for U+02BC; treating all raw variants as equivalent coverage would lose that branch.

name: normalizeIdentifier returns stable snake-case identifiers
evidence: Stable underscore encoding and both null/undefined→empty are independently observed at normalizeIdentifier. Dropping null handling or retaining spaces fails; category normalization short-circuits falsy inputs and cannot protect this direct nullable contract.

name: tokenizeProductName returns normalized searchable product-name tokens
evidence: Exact normalized token arrays preserve search words/order and prevent empty-token leakage for hyphenated Garnier, apostrophe Loreal and numbered Olaplex. Returning one normalized string or dropping the numeric token fails independently of scalar-normalization equality tests. Matcher ranking uses these arrays.

name: cleanProductDisplayName removes exact brand and product line prefixes conservatively
evidence: Five full display-cleaning cases retain two successive exact-prefix removal, unmatched line preservation, middle-word nonremoval, no Olaplexx partial-token strip and accented brand equivalence. No single existing lookup keeper reproduces all of this union. Changing prefix equality to startsWith would strip Olaplexx.

name: resolveBrandFromText returns an exact brand and product line prefix match
evidence: Legacy array/nested line aliases must resolve Nr.5 to no_5 with high confidence, exact matchedText boundary and canonical_brand_with_line_inference. Losing nested productLines or extending matchedText over product name fails; Phase0 relational fixtures do not cover this input adapter.

name: resolveBrandFromText returns an exact brand match without over-matching inside words

assertions.text: assert.equal(nonMatch.unresolvedRawText, "SK18 Leave-in Molecular Repair Hair Oil")

evidence: Canonical keeper C1: real alias K 18 resolves, while token SK18 cannot overmatch. Existing match/brand/raw assertions stay; proposed two extra assertions own the common unresolved receipt. An includes-based prefix regression still fails the negative.

name: resolveBrandFromText resolves Phase 0 aliases before canonical brand names
evidence: Relational Phase0 catalog covers canonical Pantene+line, canonical Garnier+line and line-only Fructis alias. Removing alias-first resolution or relational brand_id linkage changes brand/line/reason on one of the actual existing calls. Other corrected aliases do not preserve all these reason assertions.

name: unknown brand returns unresolved raw text with no confidence
evidence: C1: ordinary unrelated unknown reaches the same none(rawText) receipt as keeper SK18 after both prefix searches miss. Transfer confidence=none and reason=unresolved to existing nonMatch; match and exact raw echo are already asserted there. Raw literals/catalog shapes differ and are explicitly qualified in layer plan.

name: conflicting aliases are reported and excluded from usable alias resolution
evidence: Two different brands claim Shared: preserve the concrete conflict list and exclusion from usable resolution. Removing conflicts filtering can wrongly choose a brand; a generic unknown with no conflicting rows cannot catch this.

name: resolver uses Phase 0 normalized brand and line fields for punctuation variants
evidence: Canonical DB normalized fields plus straight-apostrophe/diacritics must select the same exact brand/line and preserve each raw matchedText boundary. Ignoring normalized_name fallback or token offset miscalculation escapes other alias-only inputs.

name: alias collisions with canonical brand names are reported and excluded
evidence: Alias Fructis collides with a real canonical Fructis brand: conflict reported, line alias excluded, canonical brand wins with null line and canonical_brand_exact. Dropping canonical names from conflict target map passes the alias-versus-alias test but fails here.

name: line-specific aliases with missing product lines are excluded
evidence: A line-specific alias referencing missing line must be excluded, not downgraded into brand-only alias. Pins aliases.length=0 and actual unresolved result. Removing the missing-line continue makes Elvital resolve wrongly; generic unknown does not exercise dangling identity data.

name: resolver handles corrected Phase A catalog aliases
evidence: Seven explicit corrected aliases preserve reviewed canonical targets: HairFood→Fructis, Wahre→line, Glisskur→brand/no-line, Monday→brand, Elvital, MetalDX, BaleaAqua→Professional. These are documented PhaseA operator decisions; no generic alias fixture protects all old-language compatibility mappings.

name: product identity migration creates the phase 0 identity tables
evidence: Five physical tables must be created and have RLS enabled in this additive migration. Missing one enable statement is not covered by current TS matching or the later product-visibility migration. Static syntax guard, not a claim RLS was executed.

name: product identity migration exposes only public-safe identity tables to public clients
evidence: Phase0 grants/policies expose only brands/categories, forbid writes on those and premature public lines/aliases/identifiers. Later Phase5 intentionally opens product_lines; that later contract cannot replace the historical additive migration guard. Removing the old test would lose migration-stage separation.

name: product identity migration keeps non-recommended products out of public product reads
evidence: Exact authenticated recommended-only policy in Phase0 protects replay compatibility before Phase5. Current lifecycle test reads a different migration and adds owned-product exception; it does not execute or inspect this migration. Weakening this USING while leaving successor intact is an escaped intermediate schema fault.

name: product identity migration keeps semantic product matching aligned with catalog visibility
evidence: match_products function replacement independently adds active/recommended/lifecycle filters to semantic retrieval. A correct table RLS policy does not protect SECURITY DEFINER matcher execution; omitting recommendation filter fails the literal contract.

name: product identity migration extends products without contracting legacy fields
evidence: Nullable additive identity keys, origin default/backfill/check and FK constraints must preserve legacy brand/category. Dropping old columns or forcing brand_id NOT NULL breaks historical compatibility even when modern DTO tests succeed. This whole positive/negative union stays.

name: product identity migration keeps product lines and identifiers compatible
evidence: Composite line/brand FK and partial null delete semantics coexist with identifiers per product, not global uniqueness. A globally unique barcode index would reject ambiguous evidence; scalar GTIN tests do not exercise SQL indexes or FK contract.

name: product identity migration stores script-normalized identity values
evidence: Brand/alias normalized columns stay ordinary script-normalized stored values, not generated rewrites; canonical and raw alias fields stay paired. Changing these to generated normalization would invalidate reviewed script authority independently of normalizer output tests.

name: product identity migration seeds all phase 0 product categories
evidence: Held F1: seed-membership contract is meaningful, but /'shampoo'/ scans all lowercased SQL and can match the display label after the tuple key is corrupted. No repair or deletion credit. Exact static counterexample and limits in held-findings.json.

name: product identity migration stays inside the phase 0 boundary
evidence: Migration phase boundary forbids submissions/usage/spec-table alterations. Later migration tests cannot protect accidental expansion of this historical file; introducing a spec RLS ALTER or intake table here fails. Retain cheapest independent file-level boundary guard.

name: product identity title composes brand, line and name without visible duplication
evidence: Neqi and Syoss literals have existing actual consumers, but the third branch brand=Garnier Wahre Schätze with line=Wahre Schätze exercises existing.includes(candidate), not replacement of prior shorter parts. Product-card/line helpers use a different formatter. A duplicate line emitted by composeProductIdentityTitle could escape those keepers. Whole declaration stays; no relocating one input to get credit.

name: product identity title ignores blank identity parts

assertions.text:
assert.equal(
    composeProductIdentityTitle({ brand: "  ", productLine: null, name: "Repair Shampoo" }),
    "Repair Shampoo",
  )

evidence: Blank-space brand + null line must be omitted while preserving Repair Shampoo. Existing scanResultTitle(null-brand) has a result.name fallback that can hide an empty formatter return; missing/null versus whitespace also exercises trim. No fully equivalent stronger keeper established.

name: canonical correction apply guard requires the production project confirmation
evidence: Actual registered correction operator refuses wrong confirmation and wrong exact hostname while dry-run skips apply guard. Generic apply-normalization uses a separate weaker includes guard; it cannot replace this exact correction safety test. No claims of positive DB apply or all guards tested.

name: canonical correction product patch never writes live product names or legacy fields
evidence: Actual updateProducts consumes exactly two FK columns from buildProductPatch; whole deep equality and legacy key negatives prohibit names/brand/category mutation. Returning live-name cleanup here violates explicit PhaseA constraint. No fake query runtime keeper exists for this union.

name: canonical correction alias upsert rows only include database columns

assertions.text:
assert.deepEqual(row, {
    brand_id: "brand-id",
    product_line_id: "line-id",
    alias: "Garnier Hair Food",
    normalized_alias: "garnier hair food",
    source: "curated",
  })

evidence: Actual retargetBrandAliases maps through brandAliasWriteRow before upsert; only five DB columns survive, excluding explanatory target_brand_name/target_product_line_name. Spreading the richer payload breaks DB writes despite correct display summary. Preserve pure projection contract at this registered operator boundary.
